issue.body:
## What and why

These Phase 12 tasks (`.opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md`) need a design, or for D1-026 a research package, before anyone implements them. Run each through the research workflow, commit the design, then open an implementation issue and tick the box. F12.1 (manifest) and F12.4 (provider registry) are the plan's two highest-return tasks; F12.7 (ABI spec) is part of its recommended first slice.

## Items

Each box is done when the design (or research package) is committed and an implementation issue is linked here.

- [x] **D1-019 — F12.1 Declarative world manifest (world.toml) with apply / --dry-run / diff** (L, design)
  A world.toml naming module (hash or source), seed, grants, ceilings, resource profile, roles/invites and schedules. `id world apply` reconciles a live world idempotently through existing admin operations, and `id world diff` detects drift. The plan calls it one of the two highest-return tasks.
  - Status: not started. No `world.toml` parser and no Apply/Diff command: `grep -rn 'world.toml' pkgs/id/src` finds nothing; `WorldCommand` (cli.rs:1388) lacks Apply/Diff.
  - Source: .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:31; .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:21; .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:80
  - Prerequisites: #543 — D1-011 F11.11 One client projection (seed secret, chat by scope) + enforcement test, #227 — D1-012 F11.12 Journal format version header, check and backup commands
- [x] **D1-022 — F12.4 Capability provider registry (manifested components)** (L, design)
  Providers become components with a manifest (name, version, argument schema, bounds, required scope, default ceiling), read by the ledger, compile gate and CLI, so adding a capability needs no edit to world.rs. One of the two highest-return tasks.
  - Status: not started. pkgs/id/src/world_caps.rs:55 `pub const CATALOG: &[&str]` is a hard-coded list, and execution is a string `match` in pkgs/id/src/world.rs:2526-2547. No registry type (`grep -rn 'ProviderRegistry\|provider_registry' pkgs/id/src` finds nothing).
  - Source: .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:37; .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:16; .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:80
  - Prerequisites: #540 — D1-010 F11.10 Split world.rs, world_session.rs, cli.rs (moves only), #554 — D1-013 F11.13 Error taxonomy: stable codes plus reasons on the wire
- [x] **D1-025 — F12.7 Versioned guest ABI spec, plaza_abi_version export, conformance suite** (L, design)
  Write the `plaza_*` exports and capability protocol down as a versioned spec, add a `plaza_abi_version` export, and publish a conformance suite built on F11.16 fixtures and the #239 recordings. Part of the recommended first slice.
  - Status: not started. The ABI is described only in module docs (pkgs/id/src/sandbox.rs:6-8 lists plaza_out_len, plaza_alloc, memory). `grep -rn plaza_abi_version pkgs/id` finds nothing, and there is no spec document or conformance test directory.
  - Source: .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:43; .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:84
  - Prerequisites: #544 — D1-016 F11.16 Replay self-check (`id world verify`)
- [x] **D1-021 — F12.3 Roles v2: journaled builder and moderator scopes with audit** (M, design)
  Journaled grants for builder (install modules) and moderator (revoke participants) as scope bits, with an audit record for each use; builder never gets network/file/process authority.
  - Status: not started. WorldScopes checks only CHAT/HISTORY/JOIN-style bits (pkgs/id/src/world.rs:201-204); `grep -rn 'BUILDER\|MODERATOR' pkgs/id/src` finds nothing.
  - Source: .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:33; doc/2026-10-17T08-00-00Z_feature_world_roles_directory/
  - Prerequisites: D1-019 F12.1 Declarative world manifest (world.toml) with apply / --dry-run / diff (in this list)
- [x] **D1-024 — F12.6 Structured audit log with OpenTelemetry export** (L, design)
  A structured audit log of admin actions and provider use, exported via OpenTelemetry, building on F11.7; a test replays the log to the final grants.
  - Status: not started. `grep -rn 'opentelemetry\|OpenTelemetry\|audit' pkgs/id/src/world*.rs` finds nothing. Prerequisite F11.7 has not started (D1-007).
  - Source: .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:39
  - Prerequisites: #553 — D1-007 F11.7 Host metrics, Prometheus endpoint and tracing spans
- [x] **D1-023 — F12.5 First new providers: kv, blob, http.fetch, notify** (XL, design)
  A bounded durable per-world KV store, content-addressed blobs over iroh-blobs, allowlisted http.fetch (off by default, no off-list redirects), and rate-limited notify. Each needs a ceiling, an audit entry, and bound, refusal and replay tests.
  - Status: not started. None of kv/blob/http.fetch/notify appears in CATALOG (pkgs/id/src/world_caps.rs:55-73) or in the dispatch match (world.rs:2526-2547).
  - Source: .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:38; .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:85
  - Prerequisites: D1-022 F12.4 Capability provider registry (manifested components) (in this list), D1-024 F12.6 Structured audit log with OpenTelemetry export (in this list)
- [x] **D1-026 — F12.8 Rust and TypeScript/Zig guest SDKs; WIT/component-model decision** (XL, research package)
  SDKs for Rust (wasm32-unknown-unknown) and AssemblyScript or Zig with screen/json/grid/cap helpers equal to the Roc libraries, each with an example world and a passing conformance run. Record a decision on the Wasm component model / WIT.
  - Status: not started. No sdk directory (`ls pkgs/id/sdk pkgs/id/sdks`: no such directory); all eight examples are Roc (pkgs/id/examples/{lounge,roc-chat,roc-counter,roc-grid,roc-screen,roc-world,territory,tic-tac-toe}).
  - Source: .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:44; .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:17
  - Prerequisites: D1-025 F12.7 Versioned guest ABI spec, plaza_abi_version export, conformance suite (in this list)
- [x] **D1-027 — F12.9 Program upgrade with state migration and rollback** (L, design)
  Versioned snapshots and an optional `migrate` export; an upgrade runs on a probe instance, commits only if migrated state round-trips, otherwise rolls back.
  - Status: not started. Install swaps the program and resets state handling (pkgs/id/src/world.rs:3168-3180); `grep -rn '"migrate"\|fn migrate' pkgs/id/src/world*.rs pkgs/id/src/sandbox.rs` finds nothing.
  - Source: .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:45
  - Prerequisites: D1-025 F12.7 Versioned guest ABI spec, plaza_abi_version export, conformance suite (in this list)
- [x] **D1-028 — F12.10 Fair cross-world scheduling, per-account quotas, slow-client back-pressure** (L, design)
  A hub scheduler that shares fuel/CPU fairly across worlds, with per-account quotas (worlds, storage, fuel/s) and back-pressure; exit: a spinning world cannot raise another's p99 by more than 10%.
  - Status: not started. pkgs/id/src/world_hub.rs bounds only sessions and open worlds (:12); `grep -n 'quota\|fair\|fuel_per_sec' pkgs/id/src/world_hub.rs pkgs/id/src/sandbox.rs` finds nothing. F11.7/F11.8 prerequisites are not started.
  - Source: .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:49
  - Prerequisites: #553 — D1-007 F11.7 Host metrics, Prometheus endpoint and tracing spans, #539 — D1-008 F11.8 Benchmark harness with committed baselines
- [x] **D1-032 — F12.14 Portals: cross-world messaging granted by both admins** (L, design)
  A capability both worlds' admins grant, with bounded rate and size and an audit entry on each side.
  - Status: not started. Only host-level cross-world write toggles exist (`CrossWorldWrite`/`ForceCrossWorldWrite` in the WorldCommand enum, cli.rs:1388); there is no guest-visible portal capability in CATALOG (world_caps.rs:55-73).
  - Source: .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:56; doc/2026-10-10T04-59-57Z_feature_cross_world_access/
  - Prerequisites: D1-022 F12.4 Capability provider registry (manifested components) (in this list), D1-024 F12.6 Structured audit log with OpenTelemetry export (in this list)
- [x] **D1-035 — F12.17 Module signature trust list and compiler-version provenance** (M, design)
  Verify module signatures against an admin trust list, add the compiler version to observed provenance, journal the trust decision; an unsigned module is refused when the list is non-empty.
  - Status: not started. Observed provenance exists (`ModuleProvenance` fields at pkgs/id/src/world.rs:299, :527, :586), but world.rs:310 states it is "not a signature or a trust attestation"; there is no trust list. The plan cites PR #225, which is CLOSED; provenance reached main another way.
  - Source: .opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md:65; doc/2026-10-16T09-00-00Z_feature_world_module_provenance/; doc/2026-10-16T09-30-00Z_feature_world_module_provenance/
  - Prerequisites: #541 — D1-018 F11.18 Pinned Roc compiler for checked-in example modules + CI rebuild job

# Path to Phase 12 — the ordered work queue

**This issue is the single ordered queue for everything that must land before Phase 12 feature work starts.** The roadmap (`planning/roadmaps/id.md`) points here; the repo queue claims work in this order (packet priorities encode the same sequence); the Phase 12 epic is #534.

## How work is picked (so nobody has to guess)
1. **Tier 1 — this list, top to bottom.** Labels: `priority/high` + `now`. Queue packets carry descending priorities matching the step numbers below, so the worker claims step 1 before step 2.
2. **Tier 2 — Phase 12** (label `next`): #807 F12.1, #556 F12.2, #835 F12.3 remainder, #1061 F12.4, #1062 F12.5, #1063 F12.6, #1064 F12.7, #1065 F12.8, #1066 F12.9, #1067 F12.10, #805 F12.11, #557 F12.12, #806 F12.13, #1068 F12.14, #558 F12.15, #559 done F12.16, #1069 F12.17, #560 F12.18. Designs run through #534 first.
3. **Tier 3 — Phase 13 + ideas** (`priority/low`): #785–#790, #1070–#1073.

## The order, and why
CI trust comes first because every validation verdict below is only as good as the test signal it reads. Validations then run in phase order — each audit produces the gap list the following work clears, and the earlier phases are the foundation the later ones extend. Journal compatibility (#227) precedes Phase 12 because worlds-as-data builds on the journal format.

- [x] Step 1 — #229 Stabilize shared-state failures in Firefox E2E CI — DONE 2026-10-26 (queue worker, PR #987, issue auto-closed on merge)
- [x] Step 2 — #241 Bulk LogSync test retries a mid-stream reset instead of explaining it (flaky CI test) — DONE 2026-10-28 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 3 — #551 F11.4 fast CI lane under 15 minutes — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 4 — #1075 Validate Phases 0–8 and the platform-completion brief (audit + tests) — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 5 — #1076 Validate Phase 9: portable screens, Roc libraries, collaboration (audit + tests) — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 6 — #1077 Validate Phase 10: profiles, capability ceilings, roles, fixtures (audit + tests) — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 7 — #1078 Validate the delivered Phase 11 items (audit + tests) — DONE 2026-10-27 (queue task 1259 audit complete, issue closed with the closeout table: 7 of 9 items verified by named passing tests; F11.4 regression filed as #1401, F11.5 partial tracked in #1326, F11.10 enforcement gap filed as #1438)
- [x] Step 8 — #227 Define rollback compatibility for world profile journal entries — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 9 — #553 F11.7 host metrics, Prometheus endpoint and tracing spans — DONE 2026-10-30 (PR #1715 merged; endpoint and tracing spans)
- [x] Step 10 — #539 F11.8 benchmark harness with committed baselines — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [x] Step 11 — #542 F11.9 bytes-per-frame baseline table — DONE 2026-10-27 (PR #1429 merged after CI passed)
- [x] Step 12 — #555 F11.15 smaller example modules (wasm-opt -Os, strip, ≤400 KB) — DONE 2026-10-27 (PR #1453 merged after CI passed)
- [x] Step 13 — #541 F11.18 pin the Roc compiler for checked-in example modules and rebuild them in CI — DONE 2026-11-03 (PR #3883 merged)
- [x] Step 14 — #544 F11.16 replay self-check (`id world verify`) — DONE 2026-10-27 (issue closed)
- [ ] Continuous — #534 Phase 12 design workflow (designs land ahead of each F12 item's implementation)

## Working rules for whoever picks these up
- **One issue per validation phase is deliberate**: each audit's job is to verify its phase against its plan, add the missing tests, and **file a separate issue for every gap found** — the follow-ups are the real work list, and they join this queue by label (`priority/high` + `now` while Phase 12 is blocked on them).
- **Drop rule**: any step that proves blocked, wrong, or superseded gets parked or closed with a note saying why, and the queue moves on. Never silently stall. Closing a step as superseded is always allowed; no permission needed.
- If a step's audit finds the phase is NOT actually delivered, say so plainly on that issue and file the missing work — that is the audit succeeding, not failing.

Dashboard: org Project #4, Area `id-train`, Horizon Week. Mirrored in the Grist Program roadmap ("id — Path to Phase 12").

## F12.9 — Program upgrade with state migration

From the Phase 12 plan (`.opencode/plans/phase-12-platform-flexibility.md`, workstream C):

Versioned snapshots and an optional `migrate` export. An upgrade runs on a probe instance first (the way checkpoints already do), commits only if the migrated state round-trips, and otherwise rolls back.

**Exit:** a test upgrades a counter across a snapshot format change, and a deliberately failing upgrade leaves the old program running.

**Coordination (2026-10-26 reprioritization, per Drew):** every id roadmap item now has its own GitHub issue, and priority encodes the order: (1) the path to Phase 12 — `now` + `priority/high`; (2) Phase 12 itself — `next`; (3) Phase 13 and long-term ideas — `priority/low`. The dashboard mirrors this list (org Project "Developing Today" #4, Area `id-train`; Grist Program roadmap, Area `id`). If this item turns out to be blocked, wrong, or superseded, park or close it with a note rather than letting it stall the queue — dropping an issue is always allowed; silently stalling is not.

issue.body:
# Program ecosystem (share, fork, gallery) — Phase 14 core topic (research + design)

Filed from the next-horizons discussion #1240, decided by Drew on 2026-11-05: **all themes are planned**. This issue is the core topic for **Program ecosystem (share, fork, gallery)**. Its job is research and design — broaden the idea beyond what is already understood, set up multiple next steps, and produce implementation plans. No implementation starts here; the output is design documents and implementation issues.

## Drew's principles for everything in Phase 14 (from #1240, 2026-11-05)
- Local-first is always the goal, AND a hosted version is intended: central coordination supporting a large graph of broadly accessible objects.
- Anything built must be completely usable by others hosting a small or large server themselves. P2P-hosted worlds and data behave the same as a large hosted public server; differences live in backend scale elements and access controls.
- Users connect to each other and transfer/interact directly wherever possible, so hosted resources are an offloadable backstop, not a requirement. The app must not technically need us to function. Collaborative / shared / federated / local-first / p2p.
- Our hosted instance is essentially public; other operators open theirs only as much as they want. Publishing paths: share to a big server, publish on pkarr, or self-host. All comms through iroh on the backend; first-class clients.

## The idea, broadened
Programs are the platform's content. Today they are files you have. An ecosystem asks how a program travels: authorship, versioning, signing, forking with attribution, template worlds, install-into-a-world in one click, and updates flowing to installed copies. Broaden with the trust model first (F12.17 provenance is the foundation) and the local-first rule: a gallery is a registry like any other — ours can be public, anyone can run one, and sideloading a .roc file must always work.

## Research questions (first pass)
- Program identity: name + author key + version + content hash; what a fork records
- Install semantics: pinning vs tracking a channel; what an update may change without world-owner approval (ABI, F12.7)
- Template worlds: a world snapshot as a starting point — state, programs, roles included or stripped
- Gallery as registry: same protocol family as world discovery (T2), different object type

## Dependencies and existing pieces
Builds on F12.7 ABI (#1064), F12.8 guest SDKs (#1065), F12.9 upgrades (#1066), F12.17 provenance (#1069). Registry protocol shared with the discovery topic.

## Next steps — the version ladder
- **v1 — first-iteration design** — its own issue, filed in the same pass and linked in the first comment below
- **v2 — outline: gallery & updates** — its own issue, filed in the same pass and linked in the first comment below
- **v3 — outline: public gallery** — its own issue, filed in the same pass and linked in the first comment below
- **v4 — outline: ecosystem at scale** — its own issue, filed in the same pass and linked in the first comment below

Plus a standing rule for this topic: anything the research surfaces that doesn't fit v1–v4 gets its own issue (Drew's rule: every feature, concept, or idea gets an issue), and future investigations are listed as comments here rather than lost.

## Sequencing
Design queue order: F12.4 provider registry (#1061) and F12.10 scheduling/quotas (#1067) designs land first; Phase 14 v1 designs then run hosted worlds → discovery → agents spike → the rest. Implementation follows Phase 13. The drop rule applies throughout: anything that proves blocked, wrong, or superseded gets parked or closed with a note — never a silent stall.

## Acceptance criteria
- A research + design output exists for Program ecosystem (share, fork, gallery): design documents broadening the topic beyond the current understanding, per the Phase 14 principles in the body (local-first plus hosted coordination).
- Multiple concrete next steps are produced as implementation plans / implementation issues filed from this topic.
- No implementation starts under this issue itself (per its own charter).
